diagnostic_evidence.quote: This is a simple consequence of the fact that $X + BY$ is Gaussian and there is an affine transport map between any two non-singular Gaussians.

issues.failure_explanation: Transporting X+BY affinely gives A'(X+BY)+c = A'X + A'BY + c, so the y-coefficient becomes A'B, not B. The claim is false as stated. Counterexample: n=m=1, X,Y independent N(0,1), B=2. Cov(X+2Y)=5 is nonsingular, but Var(aX+2Y) = a^2+4 >= 4 > 1 = Var(X|Y), so no a, c give an exact map.

failure_location.quote: for every choice of $B$ (assuming $\Cov(X+BY)$ has full rank for all $y_\star$) there are $A$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace with: for every B (with Cov(X+BY) nonsingular) there exist A, c such that A(x+By)+c is exact; or restrict the range of admissible B.
issues.overall_effect: The stated mechanism for non-uniqueness of exact maps for Gaussians is wrong for large B. The qualitative conclusion that infinitely many exact maps exist survives.
issues.title: False claim that every B admits A, c giving an exact map for Gaussians
issues.why_classification: This is a local rewording of a motivational remark. No result or later argument depends on the literal claim.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: $\lambda$-decomposability for a random variable $U$ with characteristic function $\phi_U$ is easily violated

issues.failure_explanation: S_dec only requires some lambda. Unif[-1,1] is 1/2-decomposable, since sin t/t = (sin(t/2)/(t/2)) cos(t/2), i.e. U =d U/2 + eps/2 with Rademacher eps. A Dirac mass is lambda-decomposable for every lambda. The cited examples therefore do not illustrate that the condition is easily violated.

failure_location.quote: characteristic functions with zeroes (e.g. uniform distribution, atoms, etc.)

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Remove or replace the examples with distributions that are provably not lambda-decomposable for any |lambda|<1.
issues.overall_effect: The heuristic justification that S_dec is small and non-generic rests on incorrect examples. With Z uniform and Y Rademacher, pi lies in S_dec.
issues.title: Wrong examples of distributions violating lambda-decomposability
issues.why_classification: This is an illustrative remark only. The formal results are unaffected and a local correction suffices.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: the EnKU is near-optimal for exact distributional conditioning beyond the Gaussian setting
in the same sense as our earlier symmetry classes

issues.failure_explanation: No smallness or genericity result for S_nl-dec is proved. Taking A=0, the weakly y*-dependent map L(x,y)=By+d(y*) is exact for every law X = BY' + d(Y), where Y' is an independent copy of Y. This holds for every pi_Y, every matrix B and every measurable d with d(Y) in L^2. So F, hence S_nl-dec, contains laws with arbitrary nonlinear conditional means, whereas E^EnKU only admits affine ones.

failure_location.quote: Thus, while alternative updates exist, they do not yield fundamentally larger exactness domains.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Either prove a precise smallness/genericity statement for S_nl-dec, or weaken the claims to say that S_nl-dec is constrained only through the noise law, which may equal a feature of the Y-marginal, while allowing arbitrary nonlinear regression functions.
issues.overall_effect: The headline interpretation (F exceeds E^EnKU only by a narrow class; EnKU near-optimal) is not established. Only the set identity of Theorem thm:F_char is.
issues.title: Smallness of S_nl-dec / near-optimality of EnKU is unsupported and misleading
issues.why_classification: The formal theorem survives, but the advertised near-optimality conclusion must be materially weakened or supported by a new genericity argument.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: angular mode $j \sim \mathrm{Unif}(\{1, \ldots, M\})$ with centers $\mu_j=\tfrac{2\pi j}{M}$
satisfies cyclic symmetry of some order $k \in \N_{\geq 2}$
Experiments 2 and 3 go beyond simply moment matching and feature highly non-Gaussian distributions that are contained in $\mathrm{E}^\mathrm{EnKU}$.

issues.failure_explanation: In Experiment 3, Z is a uniform mixture over 6 von Mises angular modes at 2*pi*j/6 with radius independent of the angle. Hence Z is mean zero and Z =d R_{2pi/6} Z (also Z =d -Z), so pi is in S_cyc. Then ell(x,y) = R(x - Ky) + K y* with R = R_{2pi/6} (or -I) is another exact affine map. The experiment therefore cannot illustrate EnKU uniqueness beyond highly symmetric laws. Only two specific non-exact alternatives are tested.

failure_location.quote: the EnKU is the only method that remains exact beyond highly symmetric laws (such as Gaussians)

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Rephrase Experiment 3 as comparing against specific non-exact alternatives, or use a non-symmetric law (e.g. unequal mode weights or non-equispaced angles).
issues.overall_effect: The empirical support claimed for the uniqueness message is overstated for Experiment 3.
issues.title: Ring-density experiment lies in S_cyc, contradicting its stated purpose
issues.why_classification: The defect concerns the interpretation of one experiment and is fixed by rewording or a changed test law. The theory is unaffected.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: $w^\top = p^\top A_s$, $v^\top = p^\top P_s$ we can rewrite

issues.failure_explanation: With A_s = P_s A P_s as an n x n matrix, eigenvalue 0 (which satisfies |lambda|<1) has left eigenvectors in ker(P_s^T) whenever V_r + V_u is nontrivial. For such p, v = P_s^T p = 0, so the derived identity is vacuous and gives no contradiction. The proof needs v != 0, not p != 0.

failure_location.quote: Say $V_s$ is nontrivial, then there is a nonzero eigenvector $p$ of $A_s^\top$ with eigenvalue $|\lambda| < 1$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Choose p as a left eigenvector of A for an eigenvalue of A restricted to V_s (so p^T P_s = p^T != 0), and state the identity in distribution with v = p.
issues.overall_effect: The inclusion of F minus S_nl-dec in E^EnKU is not validly argued as written.
issues.title: Eigenvector choice in proof of F_char may give v = 0 (no contradiction)
issues.why_classification: This is a one-line choice-of-vector fix with no change to the statement or the method.
